EvidenceBody: A recurrent public-interview question put to an individual or the whole assembly after a saying, action, quotation, or case has been raised. Linji Yixuan asks how an unnamed participant understands the four stated uses of a shout and answers the participant’s hesitation with a shout. Wufeng Ziqi asks, ‘How do you understand it?’ (你作麼生會); the unnamed respondent shouts, and Wufeng says ‘not yet’ (未在) before asking what comes after one shout or two. In a whisk case, Ganzi Xingzhe asks how a visitor understands Guishan Lingyou’s intention in raising the whisk; the offered account is rejected with ‘You had better return to Guishan’ (且歸溈山去好). Cuiyan Shouzhi says that National Teacher Huizhong and his attendant both still lacked understanding and asks, ‘How do you understand it now?’ (如今作麼生會). Yunju Shun similarly reopens the Puyan–Samantabhadra case for the assembly. The phrase demands an answer that can itself be answered, rejected, or tested in public; the texts do not define it as silent inward comprehension.
